title: In vitro RNA Cleavage Assays to Characterize IRE1-dependent RNA Decay
author: G. Elif Karagöz
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML

steps.title: Prepare all required buffers
steps.instruction: Make the following RNase‑free solutions using molecular‑biology grade reagents and RNase‑free water: • SF21 cell lysis buffer: 20 mM HEPES pH 7.4, 600 mM KCl, 2 mM MgCl₂, 10 % glycerol, 10 mM imidazole, add freshly‑prepared cOmplete EDTA‑free protease inhibitor cocktail. • IRE1 dialysis buffer: 20 mM HEPES pH 7.4, 300 mM KCl, 2 mM MgCl₂, 5 % glycerol, 1 mM TCEP‑HCl. • RNA gel extraction buffer: 300 mM NaOAc pH 5.5, 1 mM EDTA, add recombinant RNasin RNase inhibitor just before use. • RNA resuspension buffer: 20 mM HEPES pH 7.4, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM MgCl₂. • 2× RNA cleavage buffer: 40 mM HEPES pH 7.4, 200 mM NaCl, 2 mM MgCl₂, 10 % glycerol, 2 mM TCEP‑HCl. • Stop solution: 10 M urea, 0.1 % SDS, 1 mM EDTA, 0.01 % xylene cyanol, 0.01 % bromophenol blue. Store all buffers on ice or at 4 °C until needed.

steps.title: Grow and infect SF21 cells
steps.instruction: Culture SF21 cells in SF‑900 II SFM medium supplemented with 10 % heat‑inactivated FBS and 1× antibiotic‑antimycotic solution (100 U ml⁻¹ penicillin, 100 µg ml⁻¹ streptomycin, 250 ng ml⁻¹ amphotericin B) at 28 °C in Erlenmeyer flasks shaking at 150 rpm. When cultures reach mid‑log phase (1 × 10⁶–2 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹), infect with high‑titer baculovirus stock.

steps.title: Harvest and optionally freeze cell pellets
steps.instruction: 72–96 h post‑infection, collect cells into 50 ml conical tubes and centrifuge at 160 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. Either flash‑freeze the pellet and store at –80 °C or proceed directly to lysis.

steps.title: Lyse cells and clarify lysate
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet from ~250 ml culture (≈5 ml dry volume) in 20 ml ice‑cold SF21 cell lysis buffer. Keep on ice and pass once through an Emulsiflex homogenizer set to 16 000 psi. Keep the homogenate on ice and centrifuge at 30 500 × g for 40 min at 4 °C in an SS‑34 rotor. Collect the clarified supernatant.

steps.title: Purify IRE1 by HisTrap chromatography
steps.instruction: Equilibrate a 5 ml HisTrap HP column with SF21 cell lysis buffer on an FPLC kept cold. Load the clarified lysate at 2 ml min⁻¹. Wash with 20 column volumes of lysis buffer at 5 ml min⁻¹. Elute with a linear imidazole gradient from 0 to 500 mM over 15 column volumes in the same buffer. Analyze 5 µl of each fraction by SDS‑PAGE, pool fractions containing IRE1‑KR43.

steps.title: Remove His‑tag with TEV protease
steps.instruction: Dialyze the pooled protein against IRE1 dialysis buffer while adding TEV protease (250 µl of 0.5 mg ml⁻¹) and incubate overnight (12–16 h) at 4 °C.

steps.title: Polish IRE1 by second HisTrap and SEC
steps.instruction: Load the TEV‑treated sample onto a second HisTrap HP column equilibrated with IRE1 dialysis buffer to capture uncleaved protein and impurities; collect the flow‑through containing tag‑free IRE1. Further purify by size‑exclusion chromatography on a HiLoad 16/600 Superdex 200 column pre‑equilibrated with dialysis buffer, using 2 column volumes of buffer as per the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Concentrate and aliquot purified IRE1
steps.instruction: Concentrate the SEC‑purified IRE1‑KR43 to 50 µM using an Amicon Ultra‑15 centrifugal filter (30 kDa cutoff). Aliquot 25 µl portions, flash‑freeze in liquid nitrogen, and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Generate DNA templates for transcription
steps.instruction: Prepare DNA templates either as PCR products (using Phusion high‑fidelity polymerase) or as linearized pUC19 plasmids cut downstream of the RNA‑coding region. Use 1 µg of gel‑purified DNA per transcription; therefore start with at least 2 µg of PCR product or plasmid to compensate for losses. Forward primer: T7 promoter 5′‑TAATACGACTCACTATAG(N₁₄₋₂₁)‑3′; reverse primer is gene‑specific.

steps.title: Purify and quantify DNA templates
steps.instruction: Run the PCR or restriction‑digested DNA on a 1 % agarose gel, excise the correct band and purify with the QIAquick PCR & Gel Cleanup kit (elute with 30 µl buffer). Perform a second clean‑up with the Zymo DNA Clean‑and‑Concentrator‑5 kit (elute with 6 µl). Measure concentration with a microvolume spectrophotometer and adjust to 500 ng µl⁻¹ (A₂₆₀/A₂₈₀ ≈ 1.8, A₂₆₀/A₂₃₀ > 2.0).

steps.title: Transcribe RNA with HiScribe kit
steps.instruction: Set up 20 µl in vitro transcription reactions using the HiScribe T7 High‑Yield RNA Synthesis Kit, adding 1 µg of DNA template per reaction. Incubate 2 h at 37 °C following the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Terminate transcription and prepare samples for gel
steps.instruction: Add 2 µl RNase‑free DNase I to each 20 µl transcription reaction, mix gently and incubate 15 min at 37 °C. Then add 1 volume of Novex TBE‑Urea 2× sample buffer, mix, heat at 80 °C for 3 min, and immediately place on ice.

steps.title: Run denaturing PAGE and stain RNA
steps.instruction: Pre‑run a 6 % TBE‑Urea PAGE gel (Novex) for 20 min in 1× TBE‑Urea running buffer. Load 2 µl of diluted RiboRuler low‑range RNA ladder in the first well, then load each sample (≈5 µl). Run at constant 100 V for 50–60 min (≈90 min for long RNAs). Stain the gel by submerging in SYBR Gold diluted in 1× TBE for 20 min at room temperature, protect from light, then image on a UV transilluminator.

steps.title: Excise RNA band and crush gel
steps.instruction: Using a sterile No. 11 scalpel, cut around the desired RNA band and collect the gel slice in a 0.5 ml RNase‑free tube (max size 1 mm × 15 mm × 5 mm). Nest this tube inside a 1.5 ml RNase‑free tube, pierce the bottom of the 0.5 ml tube with a sterile 20 G syringe needle, and centrifuge at maximum speed for 3 min to force the gel fragment into the outer tube.

steps.title: Extract RNA from gel slurry
steps.instruction: Add ~3 gel volumes of RNA gel extraction buffer to the crushed gel in the 1.5 ml tube, vortex, and incubate 1 h at room temperature with constant agitation at 1 000 rpm in a thermomixer. Vortex again, transfer the slurry to a Spin‑X 0.45 µm centrifuge filter, and spin at maximum speed for 3 min. Collect the filtrate (containing RNA) into a fresh 1.5 ml RNase‑free tube and pool filtrates from the same RNA.

steps.title: Precipitate, wash and resuspend RNA
steps.instruction: To the pooled filtrate, add 1/9 volume of 3 M NaOAc pH 5.5 and 1 volume of isopropanol. Mix and incubate ≥30 min at –80 °C. Centrifuge at maximum speed, 4 °C for 30 min, discard supernatant, and wash the pellet twice with 1 ml ice‑cold 80 % ethanol. Spin briefly to collect residual ethanol, remove it with a pipette, and air‑dry the pellet ≥10 min at room temperature. Resuspend in 20 µl RNase‑free water or RNA resuspension buffer by gentle pipetting.

steps.title: Refold purified RNA
steps.instruction: Heat the RNA solution at 95 °C for 5 min in a thermocycler, then cool at a rate of 1 °C min⁻¹ until reaching 25 °C. Keep on ice and use immediately or store at –80 °C. Measure concentration and purity (A₂₆₀/A₂₈₀ ≈ 2.0, A₂₆₀/A₂₃₀ > 2.0).

steps.title: Set up in‑vitro cleavage reactions
steps.instruction: On ice, assemble a master mix for the desired time‑course in non‑stick 1.5 ml RNase‑free tubes. Each 10 µl reaction contains: • 5 µl 2× RNA cleavage buffer, • 15–100 ng PAGE‑purified RNA, • IRE1‑KR43 at 50 nM–5 µM (final concentration as required). For a specificity control, add 4µ8C to a duplicate of the longest time point to a final 10 µM; pre‑incubate IRE1 (10 µM) with 20 µM 4µ8C on ice for 30 min before adding to the reaction. Incubate the tubes at 30 °C (thermomixer, dry or water bath) for the chosen times (30 s to 90 min) without agitation.

steps.title: Stop reactions and prepare for analysis
steps.instruction: At each time point, withdraw 7 µl of reaction and add 1 µl proteinase K solution (20 µg). Incubate 10 min at 37 °C. Then add 1 volume of stop solution, mix gently, heat at 80 °C for 5 min, and immediately place on ice.

steps.title: Separate cleavage products by PAGE and image
steps.instruction: Load 5 µl of each stopped reaction (≈1/3 of the total volume) onto a fresh 6 % TBE‑Urea gel alongside a diluted RNA ladder in the first well. Run at 100 V for 50–60 min (longer for larger RNAs). Stain the gel with SYBR Gold (1× in 1× TBE) for 20 min at room temperature, protect from light, and image on a gel documentation system. Record exposure times and use the longest exposure that does not saturate the signal.
